name: Tanrei
description: The default design system. Near-monochrome surfaces and a monochrome primary, which it shares with the grey root it extends; over them, its own colors: one accent, the keyboard focus ring; status messages on quiet tints of their hue; and code in a conventional, vivid scheme. It leaves out the components and variants it does not draw.

segmented-button.reason: One choice among several is told by what it changes: tabs where it switches the content below, radio buttons where it sets a value, a button group where each button toggles on its own.

accent.description: Tanrei's one chromatic voice: the keyboard focus ring. Declared by this system rather than fixed in the vocabulary, because which accent a product has — or whether it has one — is that product's choice.

error-quiet.description: The hue of the error palette at a low chroma: the faint tint a message of that status stands on, and the deep tone of what is drawn on it. The error palette keeps its full chroma for the status color itself.

success-quiet.description: The hue of the success palette at a low chroma: the faint tint a message of that status stands on, and the deep tone of what is drawn on it. The success palette keeps its full chroma for the status color itself.

warning-quiet.description: The hue of the warning palette at a low chroma: the faint tint a message of that status stands on, and the deep tone of what is drawn on it. The warning palette keeps its full chroma for the status color itself.

info-quiet.description: The hue of the info palette at a low chroma: the faint tint a message of that status stands on, and the deep tone of what is drawn on it. The info palette keeps its full chroma for the status color itself.

syntax-keyword.description: A purple: the language's own words — its keywords, its modifiers, its at-rules. Declared by this system without roles: it colors code and nothing else.

syntax-string.description: A green: text quoted in the code. It is near the hue of the success palette and is not that palette: a system that re-values success does not move it, and no status role reads it. Declared by this system without roles: it colors code and nothing else.

syntax-constant.description: An orange: the values that are not text — numbers, booleans and null, named constants, units. Declared by this system without roles: it colors code and nothing else.

syntax-function.description: A blue: the names of functions, and at a tone nearer the text, of properties. Declared by this system without roles: it colors code and nothing else.

syntax-type.description: A blue-green: the names of types. Declared by this system without roles: it colors code and nothing else.

syntax-tag.description: A red: what markup and style sheets address — an element's name, a selector. It is near the hue of the error palette and is not that palette: a system that re-values error does not move it, and no status role reads it. Declared by this system without roles: it colors code and nothing else.

tanrei.sys.color.error-container.reason: A status container is a faint tint of the status on the surface, from the status's quiet palette, not a tone of its full chroma.

tanrei.sys.color.on-error-container.reason: What is drawn on a status container is a deep tone of the status's quiet palette in a light scheme and a pale one in a dark scheme. Drawn the other way round, the pair is the inverse status bar and its text.

tanrei.comp.snackbar.inverse-info.contai.reason: An inverse status bar is the status bar of the other theme. These are the tones of sys.color.info-container with light and dark exchanged; keep the two in step.

tanrei.comp.snackbar.inverse-info.suppor.reason: The text on an inverse status bar is the other theme's text on its status bar. These are the tones of sys.color.on-info-container with light and dark exchanged; keep the two in step.

tanrei.comp.snackbar.inverse-info.icon.c.reason: The glyph on an inverse status bar is the other theme's status color, the one that theme draws on this bar. These are the tones of sys.color.info with light and dark exchanged; keep the two in step.

tanrei.comp.snackbar.inverse-info.outlin.reason: The edge of an inverse status bar is the other theme's status color, as its glyph is. These are the tones of sys.color.info with light and dark exchanged; keep the two in step.

tanrei.comp.code-block.syntax.color.keyw.reason: A keyword is a purple. The default system draws code in a conventional, vivid scheme.

tanrei.comp.code-block.syntax.color.cons.reason: A number, a boolean or null is an orange. The default system draws code in a conventional, vivid scheme.

tanrei.comp.code-block.syntax.color.tag.reason: An element's name or a selector is a red, from a palette of its own and not the error color. The default system draws code in a conventional, vivid scheme.

tanrei.comp.code-block.syntax.color.stri.reason: Quoted text is a green, from a palette of its own and not the success color. The default system draws code in a conventional, vivid scheme.

tanrei.comp.code-block.syntax.color.func.reason: A function's name is a blue. The default system draws code in a conventional, vivid scheme.

tanrei.comp.code-block.syntax.color.prop.reason: A property's name is the blue of a function's name, a step nearer the text in each scheme: the two are told by tone, and by where they stand. The default system draws code in a conventional, vivid scheme.

tanrei.comp.code-block.syntax.color.type.reason: A type's name is a blue-green. The default system draws code in a conventional, vivid scheme.
